reviewedProfile.description: Programmable financial infrastructure combining payments, platform services, billing and embedded finance. Its 2026 Parafin agreement adds merchant-credit capability while FedEx brings supply-chain data.
reviewedProfile.businessModel: Payments and financial software for businesses and platforms
reviewedProfile.whyWatch: Merchant financing and logistics data now meet in a single partner strategy.
reviewedProfile.strategicQuestion: Which GoTo merchant data improves credit decisions beyond payment history?

reviewedEvidence.title: FedEx Dataworks and Stripe link supply-chain signals with SME finance
reviewedEvidence.summary: FedEx Dataworks and Stripe announced a long-term collaboration using logistics signals and financial infrastructure. Their first joint solution was planned for early 2027; FedEx would also add Stripe as a payments option.
reviewedEvidence.implication: Test whether GoSend or GoBox fulfillment signals add credit value beyond GoPay merchant payment history.
reviewedEvidence.nextAction: Validate incremental predictive lift, data rights, explainability and lender economics with a holdout cohort.
reviewedEvidence.limitations: Product launch and performance were prospective. The announcement does not prove lower credit losses.

reviewedEvidence.title: Stripe agrees to acquire Parafin to deepen embedded small-business credit
reviewedEvidence.summary: Stripe agreed to acquire Parafin, which serves platform customers including DoorDash. The transaction was expected to close in coming months, subject to customary conditions and any required regulatory clearances.
reviewedEvidence.implication: Compare acquiring lending infrastructure with distributing credit through a licensed partner before expanding GoFood merchant finance.
reviewedEvidence.nextAction: Review underwriting ownership, funding source, loss allocation and integration costs; compare partner and acquisition economics.
reviewedEvidence.limitations: No consideration was disclosed in this release. Announcement does not establish completion or Indonesian licensing.

reviewedEvidence.title: Stripe brings treasury and multi-currency money management to Australian businesses
reviewedEvidence.summary: Stripe launched Treasury in Australia to combine payment acceptance, holding and converting funds, and payments to recipients. Embedded Treasury for Platforms was described as coming later in the year.
reviewedEvidence.implication: Consider a merchant operating account with Jago and Midtrans before adding standalone merchant tools.
reviewedEvidence.nextAction: Check local regulatory perimeter, settlement liquidity and whether faster availability improves merchant retention.
reviewedEvidence.limitations: Australian product availability and economics do not establish Indonesian availability.

reviewedEvidence.title: Stripe announces employee liquidity tender at $159bn valuation
reviewedEvidence.summary: Investors and a portion of Stripe capital will finance liquidity for current and former employees through a tender offer.
reviewedEvidence.implication: Separate employee/shareholder liquidity from new issuer growth capital in the capital-events map.
reviewedEvidence.nextAction: Tender completion, seller participation, share class, transaction size and corporate repurchase component.
reviewedEvidence.limitations: The $159bn number is a valuation, not funds raised or cash paid; this is not a primary funding round.

reviewedEvidence.title: Stripe supports a Microsoft Copilot shopping experience
reviewedEvidence.summary: Stripe describes payment infrastructure supporting the Copilot shopping experience.
reviewedEvidence.implication: Assess whether Midtrans merchants need agent-compatible catalog, payment credentials and checkout integration.
reviewedEvidence.limitations: Analyst interpretation; no quantified GoTo impact
